subject: Dedicated Capacity autoscale failure — Root cause, remediation, and customer next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@greenwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated Capacity autoscale failure — initial customer notice

Julia —

I want to reach out immediately about an incident that impacted your Dedicated GPU pool this morning (approx 07:50–08:05 PT). You may have observed elevated latency and a small number of failed requests while our autoscaling logic attempted to provision additional capacity and fell back to a constrained pool.

What we did right away:
- Manually scaled your Dedicated pool +2 GPUs to relieve queued requests within ~3 minutes.
- Temporarily routed burst traffic to compatible model variants in a different region to keep request success rates high.
- Opened an internal incident and started a root-cause investigation.

What we know so far (initial):
- There was a race condition in the Dedicated autoscaler when handling concurrent provisioning events under high queue depth.
- In a small subset of cases the autoscaler failed to mark nodes as "ready" after initialization, which left the scheduler with fewer usable GPUs than expected.

Immediate next steps I owe you:
1) A short timeline of events and actions (we'll attach a CSV).
2) A postmortem with RCA and corrective actions within 48 hours.
3) A mitigation plan for your account to avoid recurrence (manual guardrails and a patch).

I’m very sorry for the disruption. We understand Dedicated capacity SLOs are critical for GreenWave production workloads — I’ll prioritize transparency and concrete fixes.

If you can share an estimated window of any business-critical jobs scheduled this week, I’ll ensure we avoid any mid-job resize events.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (short timeline)

From: Julia Park <julia@greenwave.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated Capacity autoscale failure — initial customer notice

Thanks for the quick note, Hannah.

We saw ~15% higher tail latency and two retries surfaced as errors in our alerts — both happened during the window you mentioned. Our nightly ETL starts at 02:00 UTC (19:00 PT) but we also have a smaller analytic job that runs on-demand and has a tight SLA; it triggered earlier today.

Couple of asks:
- Can you confirm whether our historical usage or a transient spike caused the autoscale to trigger?
- Will Redwood provide credits for the failed requests? We’ll need that for our internal incident accounting.

Appreciate the timeline. We look forward to the postmortem.

—Julia
Director of Platform Engineering
GreenWave Analytics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: GreenWave Dedicated autoscale failure — urgent RCA/patch plan

Team —

Summary: GreenWave (GW-ENTERPRISE-42) saw a Dedicated autoscale failure this morning that resulted in elevated latency and two failed requests. Client-facing notice sent (below).

Initial findings (from logs):
- At 07:49:21 PT their queue depth crossed autoscale threshold and our orchestration started 3 nodes.
- Node initialization completed, but the autoscaler health-check flow intermittently skipped the final "set ready" transition when two provisioning events happened within a 7s window.
- The scheduler saw only 1/3 nodes ready and began queueing, resulting in observable tail latency and a small error spike.

Ask from ops/dev:
- Dev: can you confirm the health-check state machine race and provide a repro? Attach any quick fix we can push as hotpatch.
- Rishi: need a temp mitigation we can use for GW while a patch is validated (manual guardrail / pre-warming).
- Monica: coordinate customer communications and credits if warranted.

Attachments: incident_timeline.csv (draft) — please add timestamps from the infra logs.

Hannah

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 02:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: GreenWave Dedicated autoscale failure — urgent RCA/patch plan

Quick tech notes and proposed remediation: 

RCA summary (dev analysis):
- Root cause: a concurrency bug in our autoscaler health transition code. When two provisioning requests finish in close succession, the "ready" flag update can be lost if the second thread clears a transient initialization bit before the first thread sets ready.
- Trigger: queue-depth spike caused two parallel provisioning flows to happen on the same allocation group. This is rare but reproducible with our infra stress harness.

Planned fixes: 
1) Patch the health-check state machine to use an atomic compare-and-swap for the ready transition (autoscaler_patch.diff attached). This prevents lost updates under concurrent completion events.
2) Add an extra verification pass during initialization: HPC nodes will perform a gated readiness probe from the scheduler before being marked usable.
3) Add metric alerts on "provisioning_inconsistency" and increase sampling for node readiness events.

Short-term mitigations for GreenWave (Rishi to action):
- Pre-warm two replacement nodes for GW's Dedicated pool during heavy windows.
- If autoscale sees >2 concurrent provisioning events in <10s, fall back to manual scale and alert SRE.

I can get a hotfix out within the next 6 hours, then a full release in the next 48 hours after CI and canary.

—Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: autoscaler_patch.diff

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Park <julia@greenwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated Capacity incident — root cause analysis, remediation, and next steps

Hi Julia —

Thank you again for your patience. Attached is a concise post-incident report (dedicated_capacity_postmortem.pdf) and a CSV timeline with exact timestamps (incident_timeline.csv). Below is a short RCA and the concrete steps we’ve taken and will take for GreenWave.

What happened (TL;DR):
- Between 07:49:21–07:54:00 PT on 2026-03-02, GreenWave’s Dedicated pool experienced an autoscaling event. Two provisioning completions occurred within ~7 seconds and exposed a concurrency bug in our autoscaler health state transitions. As a result, 2 of 3 nodes were not marked "ready" briefly, leading to queued requests and elevated tail latency. Two requests surfaced as errors during retries.

Root cause: 
- Concurrency bug in the autoscaler readiness transition that allows a late-clearing thread to overwrite an early "ready" set when provisioning events overlap. This happens in rare, high-concurrency provisioning scenarios.

Immediate corrective actions completed:
- We manually scaled your Dedicated pool (+2 GPUs) to relieve the queue within ~3 minutes.
- Deployed a hotfix to the autoscaler code path that serializes the ready-set using an atomic CAS (hotfix deployed and canaried against non-prod traffic).
- Added a short-term scheduler verification pass so nodes must report readiness to the scheduler before being counted toward capacity.

Planned / longer-term items (by priority):
1) Full release with additional tests and metrics instrumentation to be rolled within 48 hours (autoscaler_patch.diff included).
2) Alerting: new "provisioning_inconsistency" metric and alert.
3) Account-level guardrails: we’ve pre-warmed two nodes for your Dedicated pool during your peak windows and added a policy to prefer manual scale if >2 concurrent provisioning events occur within 10s.

Customer impact and compensation:
- Impact: two failed requests and a transient increase in 99th-percentile latency for ~5 minutes.
- Compensation: We will apply a service credit for the affected window equivalent to the compute cost of the failed requests. Monica will follow up with the precise credit amount and accounting entry.

Next steps for GreenWave:
- Please confirm any upcoming high-priority jobs this week so we can avoid scheduled resizes during those windows.
- We’ll follow up in 72 hours with monitoring evidence showing the hotfix stability and the final postmortem PDF attached here.

If you’d prefer a short call to walk through the timeline and answer questions, I’m available this week and can include Dev and Rishi.

Again — sorry for the disruption. We take Dedicated capacity incidents seriously and have immediate process and code changes in flight to prevent recurrence.

Best regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dedicated_capacity_postmortem.pdf, incident_timeline.csv
